questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. Gram stain shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. The most appropriate treatment for localized disease is:
questions.exp: Localized impetigo is treated with topical mupirocin, which covers both Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes. Oral antibiotics are reserved for extensive or bullous disease.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man has a single hypopigmented anaesthetic patch on the trunk. Slit-skin smear is negative. Nerve biopsy shows compact granulomas with few bacilli. Lepromin test is strongly positive (>5 mm at 28 days). This patient has:
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) presents with a single hypopigmented anaesthetic lesion, strongly positive lepromin (Mitsuda) test, negative SSS, and well-formed granulomas on biopsy. It is classified as paucibacillary leprosy.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with flaccid blisters on the trunk that rupture easily leaving raw erosions. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposition in a fish-net pattern throughout the epidermis. The target antigen is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris targets desmoglein 3 (Dsg3), a desmosomal cadherin. This results in suprabasal acantholysis, flaccid blisters, and positive Nikolsky sign. Intercellular IgG on DIF confirms the diagnosis.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with heliotrope rash, Gottron papules, and proximal muscle weakness. CPK is markedly elevated. To confirm the specific diagnosis and assess disease extent, the gold standard investigation is:
opts: Skin biopsy showing vacuolar interface changes
questions.exp: Muscle biopsy showing perifascicular atrophy is the gold standard for confirming dermatomyositis. Anti-Jo-1 is associated with antisynthetase syndrome. Skin biopsy can support diagnosis but is not confirmatory.

questions.q: A farmer presents with a painless nodule on the foot slowly enlarging over 3 years. Multiple sinuses discharge black granules. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Black grain mycetoma is caused by Madurella mycetomatis, a true fungus (eumycetoma). White/yellow grains suggest actinomycetoma (Actinomadura, Nocardia, Streptomyces). The distinction matters as eumycetoma requires antifungals while actinomycetoma needs antibiotics.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis. VDRL titre is 1:32. Which test is MOST specific to confirm syphilis?
questions.exp: FTA-ABS is the most specific treponemal confirmatory test for syphilis. VDRL, RPR, and TRUST are non-treponemal (reagin) tests used for screening and monitoring treatment response. Treponemal tests remain positive lifelong even after treatment.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman has grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the lips, recurring every 2 months. The herpes virus responsible for recurrences remains latent in:
questions.exp: HSV-1, which causes herpes labialis (cold sores), establishes latency in the trigeminal (Gasserian) ganglion. HSV-2 (genital herpes) is latent in sacral dorsal root ganglia (S2-S4). Reactivation occurs with triggers like UV, stress, or fever.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman has a pigmented lesion on her back. Excision biopsy shows melanoma with Breslow thickness 0.9 mm, no ulceration, and mitotic rate 0/mm². According to AJCC 8th edition staging, this is:
questions.exp: T1a melanoma: Breslow thickness ≤1.0 mm, no ulceration, and mitotic rate <1/mm². T1b requires either ulceration or mitotic rate ≥1/mm². T2a is 1.01-2.0 mm without ulceration. T2b is 1.01-2.0 mm with ulceration.

questions.q: On dermoscopy of a seborrheic keratosis, which combination of structures is most characteristic?
questions.exp: Seborrheic keratosis characteristically shows milia-like cysts (white/yellowish round globules) and comedo-like openings (follicular plugs) on dermoscopy. Blue-white veil suggests melanoma; arborizing vessels in BCC; lacunae in hemangioma.

questions.q: A lepromatous leprosy patient on dapsone develops sudden pallor, jaundice, and dark urine. Peripheral smear shows bite cells and Heinz bodies. The most likely underlying mechanism is:
opts: Oxidative hemolysis due to G6PD deficiency
questions.exp: Dapsone causes dose-dependent oxidative hemolysis, markedly exacerbated in G6PD deficiency. Heinz bodies represent denatured hemoglobin precipitates. G6PD levels should be checked before starting dapsone. All patients on dapsone develop some degree of hemolysis and methemoglobinemia.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man with severe plaque psoriasis on long-term methotrexate undergoes liver biopsy showing grade IIIA changes (moderate fibrosis, some septa). The most appropriate management is:
opts: Reduce MTX dose by 50% and continue
Switch to ciclosporin temporarily then restart MTX
questions.exp: Roenigk grading for MTX hepatotoxicity: Grade I-IIA = continue with monitoring; Grade IIB = stop and reassess after normalization; Grade IIIA or above = discontinue methotrexate permanently. Grade IIIA indicates significant fibrosis with bridging.

questions.q: A 3-year-old presents with intensely pruritic oozing plaques on the cheeks and antecubital fossae. Serum IgE is markedly elevated. Filaggrin gene (FLG) mutations are detected on genetic testing. The primary pathophysiological defect in this condition is:
opts: Epidermal barrier dysfunction leading to allergen sensitization
Primary IgA deficiency with secondary bacterial colonization
Mast cell hyperplasia with IgE-mediated type I hypersensitivity
questions.exp: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is primarily caused by epidermal barrier dysfunction due to filaggrin gene mutations. This allows allergen penetration, triggering a Th2-predominant immune response with elevated IgE. The 'outside-in' hypothesis: barrier failure precedes sensitization.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman has brown patches on the cheeks and upper lip, worsened by sun exposure. Wood's lamp examination shows accentuation of pigmentation. This indicates the melanin is located in:
questions.exp: Wood's lamp (365 nm UV) accentuates epidermal pigmentation because melanin in the epidermis absorbs more UV. Dermal pigmentation shows no enhancement under Wood's lamp. Mixed-type melasma shows partial enhancement, which is the most common type.

questions.q: A borderline lepromatous (BL) leprosy patient develops sudden swelling and erythema of pre-existing skin lesions 6 weeks after starting WHO multibacillary MDT. New tender nodules are absent. Nerve tenderness is present. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction occurs in borderline leprosy (BT, BB, BL) and manifests as swelling/erythema of existing lesions with acute neuritis. ENL (Type 2) presents with new tender nodules and systemic features, occurring only in BL/LL leprosy.

questions.q: An HIV-positive patient on HAART presents with intensely pruritic papules on the trunk and extremities. CD4 count is 80 cells/μL. Skin biopsy shows eosinophilic infiltration around hair follicles with spongiosis. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: HIV-associated eosinophilic folliculitis occurs when CD4 count drops below 200 cells/μL. Characteristic biopsy shows eosinophilic infiltration around follicles. It is intensely pruritic and responds to phototherapy, itraconazole, or antiretroviral optimization.

questions.q: An 80-year-old man has tense blisters arising from urticarial plaques on the flexures and thighs. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermal-epidermal junction. The target autoantigens (BP180 and BP230) are located in:
opts: Lamina densa of the basement membrane
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) targets hemidesmosomal proteins: BP180 (type XVII collagen, NC16A domain) and BP230. Blister forms in the lamina lucida. Tense blisters from urticarial bases with linear IgG/C3 on DIF is the classic presentation.

questions.q: A 42-year-old woman has Raynaud phenomenon, puffy fingers, telangiectasia, and skin thickening limited to the fingers and face for 8 years. Echocardiography shows pulmonary arterial hypertension. Which antibody is most likely positive?
questions.exp: Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc/CREST syndrome) is associated with anti-centromere antibody and has a strong association with pulmonary arterial hypertension. Anti-Scl70 is seen in diffuse cutaneous SSc (dcSSc) with interstitial lung disease. Anti-RNA pol III is associated with renal crisis.

questions.q: A 60-year-old farmer has a pearly nodule on the nose with rolled, translucent borders and telangiectasia. Biopsy shows islands of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and stromal retraction artifact. The most common subtype of this tumor worldwide is:
questions.exp: Nodular BCC is the most common subtype (60-80%), presenting as a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasia and rolled borders. Histology shows peripheral palisading and stromal retraction ('lacunae'). Morpheaform BCC has the highest recurrence rate.

questions.q: A patient has recurrent mucocutaneous Candida infections since childhood and markedly elevated IgE (Hyper-IgE syndrome). Investigations reveal a STAT3 loss-of-function mutation. Which cytokine pathway is primarily defective, impairing antifungal immunity?
questions.exp: Th17 cells are critical for mucocutaneous antifungal immunity through IL-17A and IL-22 production. STAT3 mutations impair Th17 differentiation, causing deficient IL-17 signaling. This leads to chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis (CMC) as seen in Hyper-IgE syndrome.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man develops multiple flat wart-like lesions on the face and trunk since childhood. HPV typing identifies HPV type 5. This clinical scenario is most consistent with:
questions.exp: Epidermodysplasia verruciformis (EV) is associated with HPV 5 and HPV 8 (EV-specific HPV types) due to mutations in EVER1/EVER2 (TMC6/TMC8) genes. Lesions resemble flat warts and have a high risk of SCC transformation on sun-exposed areas. Caused by impaired cell-mediated immunity to specific HPV types.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman on isotretinoin 0.5 mg/kg/day for severe nodulocystic acne develops acne fulminans-like worsening with new painful cysts and fever at week 4. The most appropriate next step is:
opts: Discontinue isotretinoin and switch to oral antibiotics
Continue isotretinoin and add systemic corticosteroids (prednisolone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day)
Add topical tretinoin to enhance efficacy
questions.exp: Initial isotretinoin-induced flare (acne fulminans-like) is managed by continuing isotretinoin at a reduced dose AND adding systemic corticosteroids (prednisolone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day). Stopping isotretinoin is not recommended. Steroids should be tapered over 4-6 weeks as isotretinoin is gradually increased.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis failing methotrexate is started on ustekinumab. This biologic agent targets:
opts: The p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23
The p19 subunit of IL-23 specifically
questions.exp: Ustekinumab is an anti-IL-12/23 antibody that targets the p40 subunit shared by both IL-12 and IL-23, thereby inhibiting Th1 and Th17 pathways. Guselkumab/risankizumab/tildrakizumab target the p19 subunit (IL-23 specific). Secukinumab/ixekizumab target IL-17A; bimekizumab targets IL-17A and IL-17F.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man with longstanding varicose veins has a non-healing ulcer on the medial malleolus for 4 months. Sloping edges, fibrinous base, surrounding lipodermatosclerosis. ABPI is 0.95. Cornerstone of treatment is:
opts: Split-thickness skin grafting as primary treatment
questions.exp: Compression therapy (four-layer bandaging achieving 40 mmHg at ankle) is the cornerstone of venous leg ulcer treatment. ABPI >0.8 confirms adequate arterial perfusion and makes compression safe. Skin grafting may be needed for large/refractory ulcers after compression.

questions.q: A 28-year-old athlete has scaling, maceration, and intense pruritus in the 4th toe web space. KOH mount shows septate hyphae. First-line topical treatment for tinea pedis is:
opts: Terbinafine 1% cream applied twice daily for 1 week
Clotrimazole 1% cream applied twice daily for 4 weeks
Ciclopirox olamine gel applied once daily
questions.exp: Terbinafine 1% cream is the preferred first-line topical treatment for tinea pedis due to its fungicidal activity against dermatophytes. It has a shorter treatment duration (1-2 weeks) compared to azoles (clotrimazole, which are fungistatic and require 4 weeks). Interdigital tinea pedis responds well to topical therapy.

questions.q: Skin biopsy from a lichen planus lesion shows several characteristic features. Which of the following is NOT a histological feature of lichen planus?
opts: Hyperkeratosis without parakeratosis and wedge-shaped hypergranulosis
Band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the DEJ with Civatte bodies
Suprabasal acantholysis with 'tombstoning' of basal cells
questions.exp: Suprabasal acantholysis with 'tombstoning' is characteristic of pemphigus vulgaris, NOT lichen planus. Lichen planus histology: hyperkeratosis without parakeratosis, wedge-shaped hypergranulosis, saw-toothing of rete ridges, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, and Civatte (colloid/hyaline) bodies from apoptotic basal cells.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child has intensely pruritic papules in web spaces, wrists, and genitalia, worse at night. Multiple family members are affected. Which treatment is both safe and effective for this age group?
opts: Benzyl benzoate 25% emulsion applied for 24 hours
questions.exp: Permethrin 5% cream is the treatment of choice for scabies in children above 2 months of age. Lindane is contraindicated due to neurotoxicity (especially in children and pregnant women). Ivermectin is not approved for children <15 kg. Benzyl benzoate 25% is too irritating for children.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman meets diagnostic criteria for SLE. Among the following antibodies found positive, which has the HIGHEST specificity for SLE?
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) has the highest specificity (~99%) for SLE though low sensitivity (~25%). Anti-dsDNA is also highly specific (~95%) and correlates with lupus nephritis activity. Anti-histone is associated with drug-induced lupus. Anti-Ro/SSA is seen in Sjogren's syndrome and neonatal lupus.

questions.q: A 70-year-old renal transplant recipient on immunosuppression develops a rapidly growing crateriform nodule with a central keratinous plug on the forearm over 6 weeks. Histology shows well-differentiated squamous epithelium with abrupt central keratinization. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma presents as a rapidly growing (weeks), crateriform nodule with central keratinous plug, especially in immunosuppressed patients and sun-exposed skin. It may spontaneously involute in immunocompetent patients but in transplant recipients behaves more aggressively. Many consider it a variant of well-differentiated SCC requiring excision.

questions.q: During patch testing for chronic hand dermatitis, a 72-hour reading shows erythema, infiltration, and discrete papules confined to the test site without vesicles. According to the ICDRG grading system, this is classified as:
opts: Weak positive (+): non-vesicular infiltrated erythema with papules
Strong positive (++): erythematous, vesicular, spreading reaction
questions.exp: ICDRG patch test grading: +/- (doubtful) = faint erythema only; + (weak positive) = erythema, infiltration, possible papules; ++ (strong positive) = vesicles, papules spreading beyond test site; +++ (extreme positive) = coalescing vesicles/bullae, spreading, ulceration. An irritant reaction (IR) shows glazed erythema/pustules without papules.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman at 28 weeks of pregnancy presents with chronic urticaria significantly affecting her quality of life. Which second-generation antihistamine is considered SAFEST and is preferred in pregnancy?
questions.exp: Loratadine is the preferred antihistamine in pregnancy (older FDA Category B) with the most reassuring safety data from epidemiological studies. Hydroxyzine should be avoided near term (neonatal withdrawal) and first trimester. Fexofenadine has less human data. Cetirizine is also acceptable but has limited pregnancy data compared to loratadine.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the T6 dermatome, crossing the midline only slightly. She is otherwise healthy. The treatment that reduces the risk of post-herpetic neuralgia most effectively when started within 72 hours is:
opts: Topical acyclovir 5% cream applied 5 times daily
Oral acyclovir 800 mg 5 times daily for 7 days
Oral valacyclovir 1000 mg three times daily for 7 days
questions.exp: Valacyclovir (the L-valyl ester prodrug of acyclovir) achieves 3-5 times higher bioavailability than oral acyclovir. When started within 72 hours of rash onset, valacyclovir 1000 mg TID × 7 days reduces duration, severity, and the risk of post-herpetic neuralgia more effectively than standard oral acyclovir, with simpler dosing (3 times vs 5 times daily).
